The [United Nations](United_Nations "United Nations") uses three definitions for what constitutes a city, as not all cities in all jurisdictions are classified using the same criteria. Cities may be defined as the [cities proper](City_proper "City proper"), the extent of their [urban area](Urban_area "Urban area"), or their [metropolitan regions](Metropolitan_area "Metropolitan area").

## Definitions

### City proper (administrative)

Main article: [City proper](City_proper "City proper")

A city can be defined by its administrative boundaries, otherwise known as [city proper](City_proper "City proper"). <UNICEF> defines city proper as, "the population living within the administrative boundaries of a city or controlled directly from the city by a single authority." A city proper is a locality defined according to legal or political boundaries and an administratively recognised urban status that is usually characterised by some form of [local government](Local_government "Local government").[[1]](List_of_largest_cities#cite_note-wup2007-1)[[2]](List_of_largest_cities#cite_note-2)[[3]](List_of_largest_cities#cite_note-3) Cities proper and their boundaries and population data may not include suburbs.[[4]](List_of_largest_cities#cite_note-wup2003-4)

The use of city proper as defined by administrative boundaries may not include suburban areas where an important proportion of the population working or studying in the city lives.[[4]](List_of_largest_cities#cite_note-wup2003-4) Because of this definition, the city proper population figure may differ greatly from the urban area population figure, as many cities are amalgamations of smaller municipalities (Australia), and conversely, many Chinese cities govern territories that extend well beyond the core urban area into suburban and rural areas.[[5]](List_of_largest_cities#cite_note-5) The Chinese municipality of <Chongqing>, which is the largest city proper in the world by population, comprises a huge administrative area of 82,403 km2, around the size of <Austria>. However, more than 70% of its 30-million population are actually agricultural workers living in a [rural setting](Rural_area "Rural area").[[6]](List_of_largest_cities#cite_note-6)[[7]](List_of_largest_cities#cite_note-7)

### Urban area

Main article: [Urban area](Urban_area "Urban area")

A city can be defined as a conditionally [contiguous](Geographic_contiguity "Geographic contiguity") [urban area](Urban_area "Urban area"), without regard to territorial or other boundaries inside an urban area. <UNICEF> defines urban area as follows:
> The definition of "urban" varies from country to country, and, with periodic reclassification, can also vary within one country over time, making direct comparisons difficult. An urban area can be defined by one or more of the following: administrative criteria or political boundaries (e.g., area within the jurisdiction of a municipality or town committee), a threshold population size (where the minimum for an urban settlement is typically in the region of 2,000 people, although this varies globally between 200 and 50,000), population density, economic function (e.g., where a significant majority of the population is not primarily engaged in agriculture, or where there is surplus employment) or the presence of urban characteristics (e.g., paved streets, electric lighting, sewerage).

According to <Demographia>, an urban area is a continuously built up land mass of urban development that is within a labor market (metropolitan area or metropolitan region) and contains no [rural land](Rural_area "Rural area").[[8]](List_of_largest_cities#cite_note-Demographia-8)

### Metropolitan area

Main article: [Metropolitan area](Metropolitan_area "Metropolitan area")

A city can be defined by the inhabitants of its [demographic](Demography "Demography") population, as by [metropolitan area](Metropolitan_area "Metropolitan area"), or [labour market](Labour_economics "Labour economics") area. UNICEF defines metropolitan area as follows:
> A formal local government area comprising the urban area as a whole and its primary commuter areas, typically formed around a city with a large concentration of people (i.e., a population of at least 100,000). In addition to the city proper, a metropolitan area includes both the surrounding territory with urban levels of residential [density](Population_density "Population density") and some additional lower-density areas that are adjacent to and linked to the city (e.g., through frequent transport, road linkages or commuting facilities).

In many countries, metropolitan areas are established either with an official organisation or only for statistical purposes. In the [United States](United_States "United States"), [metropolitan statistical area](Metropolitan_statistical_area "Metropolitan statistical area") (MSA) is defined by the [U.S. Office of Management and Budget](United_States_Office_of_Management_and_Budget "United States Office of Management and Budget") (OMB).[[9]](List_of_largest_cities#cite_note-9) In the <Philippines>, metropolitan areas have an official agency, such as [Metropolitan Manila Development Authority](Metropolitan_Manila_Development_Authority "Metropolitan Manila Development Authority") (MMDA), which manages [Manila metropolitan area](Metro_Manila "Metro Manila").[[10]](List_of_largest_cities#cite_note-10) Similar agencies exist in <Indonesia>, such as Jabodetabekjur Development Cooperation Agency for [Jakarta metropolitan area](Jakarta_metropolitan_area "Jakarta metropolitan area").[[11]](List_of_largest_cities#cite_note-11)

**Shanghai** (/ʃæŋˈhaɪ/;[[16]](Shanghai#cite_note-16) [Chinese](Chinese_language "Chinese language"): 上海; [pinyin](Pinyin "Pinyin"): *Shànghǎi*, Wu Chinese pronunciation: [zɑ̃̀.hɛ́] [](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/8/89/Zh-wuu-2-%E4%B8%8A%E6%B5%B7.opus/Zh-wuu-2-%E4%B8%8A%E6%B5%B7.opus.mp3)ⓘ, [Standard Mandarin](Standard_Chinese "Standard Chinese") pronunciation: [ʂâŋ.xàɪ] [](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/7/73/Zh-Shanghai.ogg/Zh-Shanghai.ogg.mp3)ⓘ) is one of the four [direct-administered municipalities](Direct-administered_municipalities_of_China "Direct-administered municipalities of China") of the [People's Republic of China](China "China") (PRC).[[lower-alpha 1]](Shanghai#cite_note-19) The city is located on the southern [estuary](Estuary "Estuary") of the <Yangtze> River, with the [Huangpu River](Huangpu_River "Huangpu River") flowing through it. The population of the city proper is the [third most populous in the world](List_of_largest_cities "List of largest cities"), with 24.89 million inhabitants in 2021, while the urban area is the [most populous in China](List_of_cities_in_China_by_population "List of cities in China by population"), with 39.3 million residents. As of 2018, the Greater Shanghai metropolitan area was estimated to produce a [gross metropolitan product](Gross_metropolitan_product "Gross metropolitan product") ([nominal](GDP_(nominal) "GDP (nominal)")) of nearly 9.1 trillion [RMB](Renminbi "Renminbi") ($1.33 trillion). Shanghai is one of the world's major centers for [finance](Global_Financial_Centres_Index "Global Financial Centres Index"), [business and economics](Shanghai#Economy), [research](List_of_cities_by_scientific_output "List of cities by scientific output"), [science and technology](List_of_technology_centers "List of technology centers"), [manufacturing](Manufacturing "Manufacturing"), [transportation](Transport_in_China "Transport in China"), [tourism](List_of_tourist_attractions_in_Shanghai "List of tourist attractions in Shanghai"), and [culture](Culture_of_Shanghai "Culture of Shanghai"), and the [Port of Shanghai](Port_of_Shanghai "Port of Shanghai") is the [world's busiest container port](World's_busiest_container_port "World's busiest container port").

Originally a fishing village and market town, Shanghai grew in importance in the 19th century due to both domestic and foreign trade and its favorable port location. The city was one of five [treaty ports](Treaty_ports "Treaty ports") forced to open to European trade after the [First Opium War](First_Opium_War "First Opium War").
